Subject: Golden Harbor private offer — consortium discount request

Hi Priyom / Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Golden Harbor is preparing the final approval package for our consortium procurement committee. Two asks from procurement: one, we need a private marketplace offer for Redwood Inference (to appear in our AWS Private Offers pipeline); two, the finance team is requesting a one-time consortium discount across the first 12 months to match a competing vendor’s bundled rate.

I attached the RFP excerpt and a suggested term-sheet for reference. Can Redwood provide a scoped discount (example: 20% off list for first 12 months) and confirm marketplace listing timing? This is time-sensitive — committee meets Nov 24.

Attached: GH-RFP-2026.pdf, GH-private-offer-term-sheet.xlsx

Appreciate any expedited help.

—Sanjay

Irene, Karthik — forwarding GH request. High-priority: customer asks for a private offer + a front-loaded consortium discount (20% for 12mo suggested). Procurement deadline 11/24.

Quick notes:
- Golden Harbor is strategic in logistics vertical, potential to expand to Dedicated in 2027.
- We can publish a private offer to AWS in ~3 business days once legal/finance sign off, but discount needs Deal Desk & finance approval.
- Karthik — need marketplace constraints (min list price, public pricing rules) and whether we can apply a special-cased private-offer concession.
- Alex — can you flag for finance review (impact to revenue recognition and whether we can offer credits in-lieu)?

Next step: quick sync to approve concession % and approve the term-sheet redline.

Thanks — Priyom

Thanks for the flag — Priyom. Karthik/Alex,

TL;DR: I'm OK entertaining a one-time concession for a strategic pilot if finance can accept the revenue impact and marketplace listing is feasible within timeline. Two asks before I greenlight:
1) Legal/Marketplace constraints — Karthik, confirm whether AWS private offers allow a bespoke % discount to a single buyer in our case and any marketplace approval lag (we need target publish by 11/21 to give GH procurement a day to review).
2) Finance impact — Alex, we need a short note on immediate ARR/ACV impact and whether we should offer credits vs. upfront discounted invoice. If credits, outline how we'd report and whether we need a revenue reserve.

If both answers are yes and acceptable, I'm prepared to approve up to a 18% one-time discount for the first 12 months for this deal (DEAL-8741) and to sign the private-offer paperwork. Anything higher requires VP approval.

Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Golden Harbor private offer — consortium discount request

Irene / Team,

Marketplace/legal check: short answer — AWS allows private offers with bespoke pricing to a single buyer, but there are constraints:
- Private offer must reference an eligible listing and pass marketplace review (we need to include a public-equivalent SKU and justify the concession).
- There's typically a 48–72 hour review by AWS after submission; publishing in 3 business days is realistic if we submit today.
- We cannot advertise the same private offer publicly or bundle non-AWS-eligible services in the offer.

Operational ask for Priyom: please attach the proposed final term-sheet (redlined) and confirm the exact list price/discount math you want applied for the 12-month window. I can help prepare the submission packet to AWS.

Karthik
Marketplace & Partner Programs
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Golden Harbor private offer — consortium discount request

All,

Finance review below (summary):
- Impact: a one-time 18% discount on first 12 months of contracted spend reduces recognized revenue by $276k in year 1 (assuming projected ARR of $1.53M).
- Accounting treatment: to preserve clean revenue recognition and simplify invoicing, finance prefers issuing a net-invoice (discount applied up front) rather than post-facto credits. Credits increase complexity for our revenue reserve and audit trail.
- Recommendation: approve up to 18% net discount applied at invoicing for month 1, with the remainder of the year billed at list (or prorated monthly per the term-sheet). If Priyom wants full 12-month netted discount, finance asks for VP sign-off due to materiality.

Given timelines, I'm ok to sign off on the 18% net discount applied at invoice if legal/marketplace confirms we can structure the AWS private offer that way. I'll prepare the finance sign-off memo for Irene to attach to the private-offer packet.

Alex Martinez
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
